The NMSTPP framework integrates spatio-temporal event modeling with deep learning to capture complex patterns in football match data. It defines football events as a marked temporal point process where each event carries spatial and temporal annotations. The model uses transformers to encode sequential dependencies, enabling accurate prediction of future events. The HPUS metric aggregates event-level utility into a holistic possession score, capturing both efficiency and tactical intent. These primitives enable GSI to perform Bayesian inference on event likelihoods and GSE to reason about possession dynamics. The dual nature of the model—predictive and evaluative—enables robust decision support across tactical and strategic domains. Failure modes include overfitting to training data, misalignment of event types, and breakdown in temporal resolution. The framework supports retroactive analysis and forward simulation, making it suitable for both real-time and post-match evaluation.
